offers.name: Lenovo ThinkPad P16 Gen 3 Mobile Workstation, Intel Core Ultra 9-285HX, NVIDIA RTX PRO 5000 24GB, 64GB DDR5 RAM, 2TB SSD, 16" WUXGA IPS Display, Windows 11 Pro

reviews.quote: This laptop is a local AI monster and the most powerful ThinkPad laptop — overall performance is limited by one specific factor: the low-wattage GPU.
Portability over peak performance — the P16 Gen 3 can't match the raw horsepower of Dell's thicker Pro Max Plus.
A spectacular spectacle in the mobile workstation world.

praises: RTX PRO 5000 24GB + 2TB covers huge CAD assemblies and dataset caches without an external drive
24-core 285HX sustains render/compile workloads in a fully serviceable chassis (SODIMM + dual M.2)
ISV-certified Blackwell pro drivers for SolidWorks, CATIA, DaVinci Resolve Studio
24GB VRAM doubles as a local-AI accelerator — runs 13B-class LLMs and SDXL comfortably
$3,000 off regular pricing is the only sane way to buy this tier
complaints: 2.7 kg + 230W power brick = desk-bound despite the 'mobile' label
WUXGA 60Hz IPS panel undersells a $9,458 machine for color work
Fan noise under sustained load is loud even in balanced mode
Only 64GB standard despite chassis supporting 192GB — RAM upgrade is an extra cost
No verified CA pro review of this exact config; marketplace-seller warranty terms need checking

design_philosophy: The top storage tier of the P16 Gen 3 flagship line: the same 24-core Ultra 9 / RTX PRO 5000 24GB combination as the 1TB config, with 2TB of NVMe for professionals whose project files and datasets justify it (a 3TB twin also exists). Desktop-replacement priorities throughout: sustained power and serviceability over weight or battery.
rating_notes: Same specs as entry 32 (1TB twin) with +0 storage; ratings identical, inferred per SHARED-thinkpad-p.md (no verified pro anchor: NBC bot-walled, BBY reviews empty). RTX PRO 5000 24GB → ai_ml 8.0 per task brief; ISV cert lifts creative_work/productivity. Storage upgrade doesn't move ratings.
